readerContract.humanQuestion: DeepSeek has a new model that can understand pictures. What does that change in an app I use?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Explain image understanding and the app-maker-to-model connection first, then keep the September 14 older-label switch as one proportionate technical note.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No model-name or API knowledge is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: The app is the interface a reader sees; its maker connects a model underneath. A new model capability reaches the reader only through the app built to use it.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader may use an app to discuss a photo and wants to know why a new model announcement does or does not change that tool.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short September 12 explanation of DeepSeek’s September 10 image-understanding release, with the September 14 routing note kept in proportion.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I understand the useful new capability and can tell the model announcement from the feature available in my app.

canonicalTruth.owner: DeepSeek owns the named API routing and rate statement; NewsStand explains the scope without inferring a web/app chat change.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Reopen the DeepSeek announcement before publication or if its API routing, timing, rates, or product-scope statement changes.

candidateRepairPreflight.apiScope: Only the named DeepSeek API routes are described.
candidateRepairPreflight.routing: deepseek-v4-pro requests route to V4.1-Flash from 04:00 UTC September 14 at V4.1-Flash rates until V4.1-Pro launches.
candidateRepairPreflight.chatBoundary: No web or app chat change is inferred.
candidateRepairPreflight.nonClaims: No quality, benchmark, availability, bill, or third-party integration outcome is claimed.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: V4.1-Flash can take pictures into account, while an app maker decides whether to connect that model and expose the capability in the app.
causalSequence: DeepSeek makes an image-understanding model available.
An app maker chooses which model to connect behind its interface.
The app passes a picture to that model before the answer can take the image into account.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A photo app can pass a picture to V4.1-Flash so the answer can take the image into account.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: For another model announcement, separate what the model can receive from what a specific app lets its users send.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Check whether the specific app accepts a picture and what the app says it can do with it.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: One conditional photo-app example teaches the mechanism. The future older-label switch remains one short technical note, with no repeated all-app disclaimer or generic instruction to ask IT.

discoveryChecks.question: Can any Californian use the finished AskCA assistant today?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. Sign-ups are open to eligible adult California residents, and the current official page says pilot participants will explore it in October.

discoveryChecks.question: Does searching official sources guarantee AskCA is right?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. California’s own About and conditions pages say the prototype may be wrong or outdated and important information should be checked with the actual agency.

discoveryChecks.question: Is the September 30 CalCareers feature the same event as the AskCA October pilot?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. The state describes it as a separate first departmental pilot powered by the same engine.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: A reader may mistake a paused new purchase for an automatic loss of active access, or make a cancellation that ends her access.
